## Part A — Creating Vectors: c(), seq(), rep()

```{r}
scores <- c(88, 92, 79, 95, 84)
subjects <- c("Math", "Science", "English", "History", "PE")

odds <- seq(from = 1, to = 19, by = 2)
spaced_nums <- seq(from = 0, to = 1, length.out = 5)

rep("A", times = 4)
rep(c("A", "B"), each = 2)
rep(c("A", "B"), times = 2)
```
##Question #1:
```{r}
#Set up a vector named age, consisting of 15, 28, 32, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 12, 42, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 8.


age <- c(15, 28, 32, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 12, 42, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 8)

# a. How many data points?

length(age)


# b. Find the reciprocal of age?

1 / age



# c.Assign also new_age <- c(age, 0, age). What happens to new_age?
```

##Part B — Subsetting (Accessing) Vectors
```{r}
grades <- c(88, 92, 79, 95, 84)
names(grades) <- c("Math", "Science", "English", "History", "PE")


# Access the 3rd element using positional indexing
grades[3]

# Access the 1st and 4th elements using positional indexing
grades[c(1, 4)]

# Access "Science" and "PE" together using their names
grades[c("Science", "PE")]

# Return all elements EXCEPT the 1st and 4th using negative indexing
grades[-c(1, 4)]

# greater than or equal to 85 using a logical condition
grades[grades >= 85]
```

##Part C — Vector Operations and append()
```{r}
x <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)
y <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)

x + y

x * 2

z <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
short <- c(1, 0)

z + short

fruits <- c("apple", "banana", "cherry")

append(fruits, "date")
append(fruits, "kiwi", after = 1)

##Question #8:
# The recycling rule automatically repeated the shorter vector from the start to finish uintil its lenght matched the longer vector.

##Question #9:
z <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
v <- c(1, 0, 1)

z + v
# Yes it works

z + c(1, 0, 1, 1)

#  The other recycles when the lenght of the longer vector is an exact multiple. While the one that issues a warning because the longer length is not an exact multiple of the shorter length.
```

##Part D — Lists: Creating and Subsetting
```{r}

student <- list(
  name = "Maria Santos",
  age = 20,
  grades = c(88, 92, 79),
  is_enrolled = TRUE
)

student["grades"]
class(student["grades"])

student[["grades"]]
class(student[["grades"]])

student$name

student$grades[2]
```
